text: {"memo": "As of the 2025-03-31 research note, PepsiCo’s most recently completed fiscal year was FY2024, ended 31 December 2024. FY2024 net revenue was about $91.5 billion, up roughly 5% from $86.9 billion in FY2023, with organic net revenue growth near 8.8%. Net income was about $10.7 billion, or diluted EPS of about $6.25, versus $8.7 billion and $5.10 in FY2023. Gross margin remained around 60%, operating margin was about 22%, and net margin improved to roughly 12% from about 10% in FY2023. Cash flow from operations was strong, around $14.8 billion. In FY2023, revenue was $86.9 billion, net income was $8.7 billion, EPS was $5.10, and operating cash flow was about $13.0 billion. In FY2022, revenue was $80.5 billion, net income was $8.6 billion, EPS was $5.04, and margins faced input-cost pressure. The business showed resilient pricing power, though organic growth moderated. FY2024 results suggest steady demand, strong cash generation, and improving profitability. On balance, PepsiCo looked like a cash-rich, defensive consumer staples compounder at roughly a premium valuation versus long-term growth, but the stock may need tight cash management to sustain earnings compound growth."}
